title: Every exact symplectomorphism of a compact surface with prescribed collar behaviour that is C1-close to the identity is generated by a quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian, with C1-small Hamiltonian and a collar expansion b_C + r^2 h_C
author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds
source_version: Journal de l'École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.195
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem 2.8 at source lines 584-598, label t:quasi_autonomous: every exact symplectomorphism of a compact surface whose exact two-form satisfies the author's collar Assumption and which is sufficiently C1-close to the identity is generated by a Hamiltonian isotopy with a quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian, with C1-small H_t and phi_t and with the collar expansion H_t(r,s) = b_C + r^2 h_C(t,r,s) where |b_C| and the C0 norm of h_C are small. The retained proof is source section 2.3, which first has to build the tools it needs: it normalises a primitive in each collar to (a_C - r^2/2) ds, constructs the explicit map kappa_0(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) and proves a Weinstein tubular neighbourhood lemma for the diagonal of a surface with boundary, including the identity f(z_1,z_2) = -integral over the arc [z_1,z_2] of nu_0 on the boundary, and only then analyses the generating function on the cotangent bundle to produce the quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian and its boundary expansion. Neither the existence of a quasi-autonomous generator nor the boundary shape b_C + r^2 h_C follows from the usual C1-closeness theorem: the extremal points of H_t have to be produced from critical points of the generating function, and the collar expansion has to be read off from the explicit boundary formula for psi. The C1 estimates of items (i) and (ii) at source lines 589-597 are quantitative and are not restated anywhere else in the article.
